title: Create Hello World Function
statement:
Write `createHelloWorld()`. It takes no arguments and returns a new function, and that new function must return the string `"Hello World"` every time it is called, whatever arguments it receives and however many.

Each case gives `calls`, a list of argument lists. `createHelloWorld()` is called once, then the function it returned is called once with each list in `calls`, in order, using that list's values as its arguments. The answer is the list of values those calls return. (LeetCode's own cases make a single call; a case here may make several, so a function that works only once is caught.)
constraints: calls[i][j] is any JSON value: a number, string, boolean, null, list or object
notes:
## Intuition

This is the smallest possible closure exercise. `createHelloWorld` is a **function factory**: calling it builds and hands back another function. The inner function is free to accept arguments and simply ignore them, since its result never depends on them. Storing the text in a variable of the outer function shows the closure at work: the inner function can still read `greeting` long after `createHelloWorld` has returned.

## Approach

1. In `createHelloWorld`, keep the text `"Hello World"` in `greeting`.
2. Return a new function that collects whatever arguments arrive in `args`.
3. That function ignores `args` and returns `greeting`.

## Example 1, step by step

`calls = [[]]`: one call with no arguments.

- `createHelloWorld()` runs once, sets `greeting = "Hello World"` and returns the inner function `f`.
- `f()` is called with no arguments; `args` is `[]`.
- `f` returns `greeting`, so the answer is `["Hello World"]`.

In Example 2, `f({}, null, 42)` gets `args = [{}, null, 42]` and still returns `"Hello World"`. With more lists in `calls`, every call adds the same text again.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1) to build the function and O(1) per call (gathering `args` aside).
- Space: O(1): one string kept by the closure.

## Pitfalls

- Returning the string from `createHelloWorld` itself instead of a function that returns it.
- Printing with `console.log` instead of returning the value; the answer is the return value.
- Spelling: the text is exactly `Hello World`, with a capital W and one space.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `greeting` | the fixed text, kept alive by the closure |
| `args` | whatever arguments the returned function receives; unused |

narration.1: createHelloWorld is a factory: each call builds a new function.
narration.2: greeting holds the text; the returned function will still see it after the factory returns.
narration.3: Hand back a function that accepts any arguments at all.
narration.4: The arguments are ignored: every call returns the same greeting.
narration.5: The inner function is complete; it is what the caller receives.
